clue.text: After resting, gone astray this fire-resister

indicators.note: the clue puts the strayed word after the resting piece, so it follows it

parts.note: someone resting is a-bed, lying in bed

indicators.note: gone astray means wandering off course, so the letters of 'gone' are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who has had a rest finds that something has wandered off.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Daniel, Abednego, with Shadrach and Meshach, walked unharmed out of Nebuchadnezzar's fiery furnace; 'astray' is the anagram signal on 'gone'.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical figure survived the furnace untouched by flames, so he resisted fire.

clue.text: "Wolf " crier, in the jolly manner? It's odd

parts.note: a la (French, in the manner of) plus RM, Royal Marine; a Royal Marine is nicknamed a 'jolly'

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters of 'It's' are rearranged

parts.note: the letters I, T and S

explanation.surface: A question about the merry way someone cries wolf, followed by a remark on its strangeness.
explanation.walkthrough: A LA + RM gives ALARM; 'odd' turns ITS into IST. A 'jolly' is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy who cried wolf raised false scares, the mark of a scaremonger.

clue.text: Inject with spirit ?

parts.note: read 'spirit' as bravery and 'inject' as putting it in: the French prefix en- (in) plus the word for bravery

explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to fill them with bravery, putting spirit into them.

clue.text: Wanting to see a river back in New York

indicators.note: the river is placed in the abbreviation for New York, inside its two letters
back means the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and also one on the England-Wales border

explanation.surface: Someone longing to visit a river on their way back to New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DEE into EED, which goes 'in' NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in want means lacking necessities, as the poor do.

clue.text: Set girl to make tissue

indicators.note: the letters of 'Set girl' are used to make something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Arranging for a girl to produce some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' rearranges the seven letters of SET GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartilage is a tough connective tissue, the chewy part of meat.

clue.text: Help to come clean from a predicament

definitions.meaning: to rub or scratch dirt away, helping a surface come clean
an awkward fix or tight spot

explanation.definitionFit: Scraping cleans a surface by rubbing; a tight spot is colloquially a scrape too.

clue.text: Never-ending correspondence suited the old knight

definitions.meaning: letters passed on endlessly, each recipient told to copy and send them on
the linked metal rings that a medieval knight wore as his suit of armour

explanation.definitionFit: Chain letters are post sent on and on; linked iron rings formed medieval armour.

clue.text: Merry flier with batty transport

parts.note: Shakespeare's airy spirit in The Tempest sings 'Merrily, merrily' and 'On the bat's back I do fly'

explanation.definitionFit: Prospero's servant spirit in The Tempest flies on a bat's back and sings of living merrily.

clue.text: Say, be serious, man !

indicators.note: say tells you to speak the word for serious and listen to its sound

parts.note: earnest means serious and sincere

explanation.surface: Someone urging a man to stop joking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be serious' also recalls Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest, whose pun on the name is the same one.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's given name, as in Ernest Hemingway.

clue.text: Appears in the nude in picture-stories

definitions.meaning: comic sequences of drawn panels in a newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: Undressing is stripping off; comic cartoons in a paper are strip cartoons.

clue.text: Satchel I'm repairing for a transmuter

indicators.note: repairing a broken satchel puts it back together differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone mending a school bag for a person who changes things.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval experimenters tried to turn base metals into gold, a transmutation.

clue.text: Such corn induced nostalgia in a widow

definitions.text: Such corn induced nostalgia in a widow

parts.words: Such corn induced nostalgia in a widow
parts.note: Keats's Ode to a Nightingale pictures the widow Ruth homesick, standing in tears amid foreign corn

explanation.definitionFit: Keats wrote of Ruth 'amid the ... corn', the grain of a land not her own.

clue.text: Like those feet that "stole in andout"?

definitions.text: Like those feet that "stole in andout"?

parts.words: Like those feet that "stole in andout"?
parts.note: Suckling's Ballad upon a Wedding: 'Her feet beneath her petticoat, Like little mice, stole in and out'

explanation.definitionFit: Feet compared to little mice are mouselike, quiet and timid.

clue.text: Euclidean music-makers ?

parts.note: three-sided figures from Euclid's geometry that are also percussion instruments struck with a metal beater

explanation.definitionFit: Three-sided shapes are studied in geometry, and steel ones of that shape are played in orchestras.

clue.text: Resort where a Wagnerian bird takes his time

parts.note: in Wagner's opera Lohengrin the knight arrives in a boat drawn by a swan
one's age is the time one has lived, or a period of time

explanation.surface: A holiday town where a bird from opera takes things slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: SWANAGE is a seaside resort in Dorset, on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a seaside holiday town, a place people go to on holiday.

clue.text: It's an average, we hear, for preservation by planners

indicators.note: we hear tells you the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: rephrased as 'a mean it is', since a mean is an average

explanation.surface: Someone remarking that a figure is merely average, for the benefit of town planners.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'a mean it is' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Planners protect pleasant features of a place, such as parks and open views, as things worth preserving.

clue.text: He's mad to be so mixed-up and humiliated

indicators.note: mixed-up means jumbled, so the letters of 'He's mad' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man so angry and confused that he is embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone humiliated has been made to feel disgraced and ashamed.

clue.text: Blue-penciller? The De'il'awa' wi' him

definitions.meaning: an editor who strikes out text with a blue pencil cuts it, so one who cuts out
Burns's song 'The Deil's Awa wi' th' ...', in which the Devil carries off a tax officer

explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns was himself a tax officer when he wrote the song.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-penciller cuts text out; Burns's song has the Devil dance off with a customs officer.

clue.text: Home for the Forsaken Merman

parts.note: Matthew Arnold's poem The Forsaken Merman tells of a sea-king living beneath the waves

explanation.definitionFit: Arnold's merman lives on the ocean floor, below the waves.

clue.text: Now slides the silent — on, and leaves A shining furrow" (Tennyson)

definitions.text: Now slides the silent — on, and leaves A shining furrow" (Tennyson)

parts.words: Now slides the silent — on, and leaves A shining furrow" (Tennyson)
parts.note: a missing word from Tennyson's lyric 'Now sleeps the crimson petal': a shooting star leaving a bright trail

explanation.definitionFit: The poem's silent thing crossing the sky leaves a glowing track, like a shooting star.

clue.text: Debate concerning a boy

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An argument about a young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue a matter out logically is to reason about it.

clue.text: Fountain range

definitions.meaning: the Greek mountain where the Muses' springs flowed, a source of poetic inspiration
a mountain range in Boeotia, Greece

explanation.definitionFit: The Boeotian mountains held the springs of Aganippe and Hippocrene, so the name stands for both the peaks and the poets' source.

clue.text: She's very entertaining

parts.note: 'entertaining' read as receiving guests, not as being amusing

explanation.definitionFit: A woman who entertains guests at a party is the one receiving them.

clue.text: "Some dish more sharply.--than domestic bliss "(Patmore)

parts.note: a missing word from Coventry Patmore: 'Some dish more sharply ... than this Milk-soup men call domestic bliss', a word for seasoned

explanation.definitionFit: A dish sharply flavoured with seasoning is the opposite of bland milk soup.

clue.text: Re these bargainers, they're no democrats !

definitions.text: Re these bargainers, they're no democrats !

parts.words: Re these bargainers, they're no democrats !
parts.note: 'bargainers' read as bar-gainers, innkeepers; put RE before their name and you get the American party opposed to the Democrats

explanation.walkthrough: In the US, Republicans and Democrats are the two main parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Innkeepers earn their living from the bar, so they gain from it.

clue.text: Our own railway welcomes the valorous

parts.note: BR is British Railways, the nationalised British railway
ave is a Latin word of greeting, a hail or welcome

explanation.walkthrough: BR was British Railways, the nationalised railway of the time, hence 'Our own'.
explanation.definitionFit: The valorous are the courageous, those who show daring.

clue.text: Dweller on 21 goes east for foreign culture-centre

parts.note: the Muses lived on the Greek mountain at 21 across

explanation.surface: A mountain dweller travels east to a gallery abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the French word for a museum, hence 'foreign'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is French for a museum, a cultural institution abroad.

clue.text: The prophet's made mainly of transparent stuff

definitions.text: The prophet's made mainly of transparent stuff

parts.words: The prophet's made mainly of transparent stuff
parts.note: all but the last letter of the prophet's name spell a clear mineral that splits into thin sheets

explanation.walkthrough: The prophet's name minus its last letter is MICA, a glassy mineral used for windows in stoves.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one of the twelve minor prophets of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Plantigrade, pelt, one, for the use of

parts.note: an animal's pelt is its coat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fur pelt set aside for one person's use.
explanation.definitionFit: This raccoon relative walks on the soles of its feet, as plantigrade animals do.

clue.text: When it's time for the bowler to act, he wins

definitions.text: When it's time for the bowler to act
definitions.meaning: in cricket a bowler bowls a set of six balls, called an over

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an 'over' is a set of six balls bowled by one bowler from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler acts when his turn of six balls arrives; a winner defeats his opponents.

clue.text: Like Cleopatra in her salad days?

definitions.text: Like Cleopatra in her salad days?

parts.words: Like Cleopatra in her salad days?
parts.note: Shakespeare's Cleopatra speaks of 'my salad days', and a salad wears a dressing; the word also means smartly clothed

explanation.definitionFit: Salad is served with a dressing, and smart clothes make someone well turned out.

clue.text: Debility, then, in a continent ?

indicators.note: the word 'then' is placed in the continent's name

parts.note: Asia is a continent

explanation.surface: Weakness, then, somewhere on a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' looks like a link word, but its own letters are the inner piece that 'in' places inside the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the medical word for weakness or loss of strength.
